key_insight: The paper reframes chemical source localization as a backward transport problem, using detected concentrations to infer likely emission sites through a learned backward propagator for tracer paths.
engineering_relevance: This offers a physics-informed, Galilean-invariant search strategy that can improve real-world plume tracking and robotic olfactory localization in turbulent flows.
method: Learn the backward propagator of passive tracers from flow dynamics.
Formulate source localization as a Schrödinger bridge between emission and detection points.
Sample candidate source locations with Langevin dynamics driven by the learned backward transport drift.
evidence_signal: In two-dimensional turbulence, the method is reported to outperform classical search strategies across different wind regimes using a single learned propagator.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and generalization of the learned backward transport model, especially when flow conditions differ from training data.
paper_title: Learning Backward Transport for Source Localization
